title: Create a layer and draw a circle on it
task: Create a named layer (LayerTable.FindName then Add) and add a circle on it, setting ObjectAttributes.LayerIndex so the new object lands on that layer rather than the current one.
script:
# Task: create a named layer and draw a circle on that layer.
import System
import Rhino
import scriptcontext as sc

name = "MCP Circles"

# 1. Find the layer by name, add it if it is not there yet. FindName returns the
#    Layer or None; Add(name, color) returns the new layer's index.
layer = sc.doc.Layers.FindName(name)
if layer is not None:
    index = layer.Index
else:
    index = sc.doc.Layers.Add(name, System.Drawing.Color.Blue)

# 2. Build a circle on the world XY plane, radius 10.
circle = Rhino.Geometry.Circle(Rhino.Geometry.Plane.WorldXY, 10.0)

# 3. Pin the new object to our layer with ObjectAttributes. Without this the
#    circle lands on whatever the current layer is, not the one we just made.
attrs = Rhino.DocObjects.ObjectAttributes()
attrs.LayerIndex = index
guid = sc.doc.Objects.AddCircle(circle, attrs)
if guid == System.Guid.Empty:
    raise Exception("AddCircle returned an empty id")

sc.doc.Views.Redraw()
result = "added circle %s on layer %s (index %d)" % (guid, name, index)

pitfalls.symptom: The circle is added to the document but ends up on the current layer, not the layer the script created.
pitfalls.cause: AddCircle(circle) with no attributes uses the document's current layer; creating a layer does not make it current.
pitfalls.fix: Pass a Rhino.DocObjects.ObjectAttributes with LayerIndex set to the target layer's index to AddCircle.

pitfalls.symptom: Calling Layers.Add for a name that already exists creates a duplicate or returns an unexpected index on re-runs.
pitfalls.cause: Add always appends; it does not de-duplicate by name.
pitfalls.fix: Look the layer up with FindName first and reuse its Index when it already exists.
